result:
Rules are not stored on the bundle as data. Each rule is recorded as a deferred callback during bundle setup, then replayed against the app when the bundle is registered.

1. **`Tessel.register_bundle`** (`src/tessel/sansio/app.py:571`) is the entry point. It calls `bundle.register(self, options)`.
2. **`Bundle.register`** (`src/tessel/sansio/bundles.py:273`) records the bundle in `app.bundles`, creates a `BundleSetupState` via `make_setup_state`, and runs each entry in `self.deferred_functions` with that state (line 334). It also attaches the static route if the bundle has a static folder (line 323). Nested bundles are then registered from `self._bundles` (line 349).
3. **`Bundle.attach_route_rule`** (`src/tessel/sansio/bundles.py:413`) is what fills `deferred_functions`. It calls `self.record(lambda s: s.attach_route_rule(...))`, so nothing reaches the app until registration. `Bundle.record` (line ~225) appends to that list.
4. **`BundleSetupState.attach_route_rule`** (`src/tessel/sansio/bundles.py:87`) applies the bundle's `url_prefix`, `subdomain`, and `url_defaults`. It prefixes the endpoint with the bundle name and calls `app.attach_route_rule`.
5. **`Tessel.attach_route_rule`** (`src/tessel/sansio/app.py:606`) builds the rule with `self.url_rule_class` (`Rule`) and calls `self.url_map.add(rule_obj)`. It also records the view function in `self.view_functions`.

I did not check `src/tessel/app.py`, which may override some of these methods.
